content:
# Split law + crash-resilient seat design

## 1. Semantics, pinned

- **Path H (hash/exec path):** deterministic re-execution of the block body. Fixed work `m` = number of touched state accesses (stems). Rate `B_H` = accesses/sec, CPU-bound.
- **Path P (proof/provenance path):** ingest + verify the Verkle witness bundle, sliced into uniform per-stem proof-groups. Tunable work `q` = number of groups fed. Rate `B_P` = groups/sec, network+pairing bound.
- **Rendezvous:** the provenance gate opens only when both paths finish. Set `q/B_P = m/B_H`:

```
q* = m · B_P / B_H        t_gate = m/B_H = q*/B_P
```

Finishing together (not merely ASAP) matters because the gate is a single atomic flip requiring *both* (a) provenance of every pre-image value and (b) `Δroot(R_{n−1}, deltas) == R_n`. Neither condition alone opens it; tail idle on either path is pure makespan loss against the attest deadline.

Worked numbers: `m = 24,000`, `B_H = 50k/s`, `B_P = 12k groups/s` → `q* = 5,760` groups, `t_gate = 480 ms`. Witness stream ≈ 5.8 MB ≈ a ~100 Mbps feed — consistent with `B_P` being network-bound.

## 2. q* is a control law, not a constant

Recompute it over **remainders** at every checkpoint (every `⌈q*/64⌉` P-units or 50 ms, whichever first):

```
q*_rem = m_rem · B̂_P / B̂_H
```

- Clamp: `q_run = min(q*, Q_avail)`. If the block touches fewer stems than `q*`, P finishes early; gate opens at `m/B_H`. Correct, just not balanced.
- Rates: EWMA α = 1/8; per-step adjustment clamped to ±25% of `q*` to prevent oscillation.
- **Measurement discipline:** count only *service-limited* intervals toward `B̂_P`. Starvation (no data arrived) is not slowness. Track the two separately or your split law silently mis-sizes.
- Calibration: at seat start, run a calibration block (`m_cal = 4096` synthetic accesses) → `B̂_H = m_cal/t_cal`. Recalibrate per epoch or on hardware change.
- Batch KZG verification raises effective `B_P` ~3–5×, which proportionally raises `q*`. The law absorbs it automatically.

## 3. What persists vs. what recomputes

Design rule: **persist only what is expensive to redo AND cheap to re-verify, plus monotone progress markers. Never persist unverified data as trusted. Everything derivable from anchors is recomputed.**

| Persists (durable) | Size | Why | Invalidation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Seat keys (encrypted) | — | identity | never |
| Anchors: finalized header, `R_{n−1}`, slot/epoch | ~100 B | sole trust roots | reorg → drop descendants |
| Progress journal: per-unit `[unit_id, result_digest, ver, CRC]`; H-units also carry actual post-values (32 B each) | ~3.3 MB/block | skip finished units on respawn | prune at finalize+1 epoch |
| Done-hash-chain: `h_{i+1} = H(h_i ‖ unit_id ‖ digest)` | 32 B | O(1) incremental; tamper-evident | extends across respawn |
| Death-time checkpoint sig: `Sig_seat(H(ver ‖ R_{n−1} ‖ done_chain ‖ delta_root ‖ seq))` | 96 B | converts volatile verification into self-authenticating state | per block |
| Verkle skeleton, levels 0–1, commitments only | ≤ 3 MB | re-fetch costs round trips; self-authenticating against `R_{n−1}` | root change |
| Raw witness slices, content-addressed, tagged `UNVERIFIED` | ≤ 64 MB cap, LRU | refetch beats reverification only when `B_P` is network-bound | verify-on-use, then promote or evict |
| Rate EWMAs `(B̂_P, B̂_H)` + sample counts | ~32 B | avoids one wasted cold cycle | recalibrate triggers |
| Gate receipts (signed, append-only) | tiny | provenance lineage, slashing defense | never |

| Recomputes on respawn | Source | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| `m` | rescan block body | ms |
| `q*` | law over persisted EWMAs | µs |
| Done-set bitmap | journal tail scan (CRC-checked) | ~50 ms @ 10⁵ records |
| Delta overlay / running `Δroot` | replay journaled values over `R_{n−1}` | ms-scale hashing |
| Any unit lacking a valid record | redo from `(R_{n−1}, block, witness)` | bounded by remainder law |
| Execution scratch, gas frames, partial proof buffers | — | never persisted |

Explicitly **not** persisted: `q*` itself (derived), anything unverified-as-trusted, peer heuristics feeding the split.

## 4. Crash consistency mechanics

- Record format: `[len u16][type u8][ver u32][unit_id u64][payload][crc32c u32]`. Append → fsync → mark done in RAM. Torn tail = CRC/length fail → truncate to last good record.
- H-unit records are atomic: values + digest in one record. Otherwise a respawn could apply values whose verification evidence was lost.
- **Version tag in every record.** Digests are only comparable within a code version; on mismatch, discard those records and recompute. Non-negotiable.
- Idempotence: re-execution is deterministic given `(R_{n−1}, block, witness)`, so skip-if-journaled is safe.
- Disk-full on journal append → set degraded flag, continue all-in-RAM. Gate stays sound; you just lose crash-resume.

## 5. Respawn sequence (budgeted)

```
t=0     death. Disk retains anchors, journal, chain, skeleton, EWMAs, slice pool.
t+r     r ≈ 200 ms process start
 1. Load anchors; validate against finalized checkpoint (~1 KB).
 2. Scan journal tail → done-set; truncate torn tail.
 3. Extend done-chain; verify checkpoint sig if present.
 4. Recompute m, q*_rem = m_rem·B̂_P/B̂_H; resume both paths on remainders.
 5. Gate opens when done-set complete ∧ Δroot == R_n. Attest.
```

With hit-rate ρ = 0.6 at death: `≈ 200 + 50 + 0.4·480 ≈ 440 ms` — cheaper than a full 480 ms redo. The rendezvous invariant is restated over remainders; a mid-flight death breaks the original simultaneity and the law re-establishes it.

## 6. Soundness rules binding shortcuts to the gate

Persistence is an optimization; correctness always bottoms out in `Δroot(R_{n−1}, deltas) == R_n`.

- Corrupted persisted **delta values** → wrong `Δroot` → detected → discard journal, full recompute of the block. Safe.
- Corrupted **P-digests**: with a checkpoint sig, tampering breaks the signed done-chain → detected on extension. Without a sig (SIGKILL beat the handler): either re-verify all P-units (one `B_P` pass, the rare path) or audit-sample `1/s` of skipped units — detection probability `1 − (1−1/s)^b` (s=32, b=10 bad → ~27%, too weak alone). **Commit: no sig ⇒ full P re-verification.**
- Graceful death (SIGTERM, ~50 ms handler) emits the checkpoint sig; that is the mechanism that makes respawn cheap *and* sound.
- Reorg between death and respawn → drop journal wholesale, restart from canonical anchor.

## 7. Failure matrix

| Event | Detection | Recovery | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Kill mid-P-verify | no record | redo unit | 1 group |
| Kill mid-H-exec | record absent/non-atomic | redo accesses | deterministic |
| Torn journal tail | CRC | truncate | none |
| Version skew | ver field | drop records | recompute range |
| Delta corruption | `Δroot ≠ R_n` | full block recompute | one cycle |
| Digest tamper, sig present | chain break | reject chain, re-verify | one `B_P` pass |
| Digest tamper, no sig | — | full P re-verify (policy) | one `B_P` pass |
| Reorg | anchor compare | drop journal | full redo |
| Disk full | append error | degraded in-RAM mode | lose resume only |

## 8. Steady-state footprint

Journal pruned at finalize; skeleton ≤ 3 MB; slice pool ≤ 64 MB; receipts negligible. **< 100 MB disk, zero reliance on volatile state for correctness
reasoning:
Let me parse this problem carefully. The user is asking about a "measured split q* = m·B_P/B_H" that makes two resource paths finish together, in a "verkle chain / provenance gate" context, designed for a "stateless seat that dies and respawns" — what persists vs recomputes.

This is dense jargon. Let me decode it:

- **Verkle chain**: A blockchain using Verkle trees (vector commitments / KZG-based polynomial commitments) instead of Merkle trees. Key property: stateless clients can verify state transitions with small witnesses (proofs) because Verkle proofs are O(1)-ish in width rather than O(log n) hashes. Statelessness = validators don't store full state; they verify blocks against a state root plus witnesses.

- **Provenance gate**: Some gating mechanism where an action (e.g., including a transaction, claiming a resource, entering a seat/role) requires proof of provenance — where data came from, that it's attested. Could be a gate in the sense of a check: you must present provenance evidence to pass.

- **Stateless seat that dies and respawns**: A validator/prover seat (a role in the protocol) that holds no persistent state; it can be killed and respawned (crash-recovery, or ephemeral workers). The question: what must persist across death/respawn vs what can be recomputed deterministically.

- **Two resource paths finish together**: There are two paths consuming resources (compute? bandwidth? storage?) and we want them to finish at the same time — i.e., balance work so both complete simultaneously. The split q* is the fraction of work assigned to path P vs path H.

- **q* = m·B_P/B_H**: q* is a measured split equal to m times the ratio of B_P to B_H. B_P and B_H are presumably bandwidth or throughput of path P and path H. m is some multiplier (maybe number of chunks, or a safety margin, or a measured constant).

So the design task: given two resource paths P and H with bandwidths/capacities B_P and B_H, choose a split point q* such that both paths finish simultaneously (work-conserving balance), where q* = m·B_P/B_H. Then design the persistence/recomputation boundary for a stateless seat under verkle-chain constraints with a provenance gate.

Let me think about what "two resource paths" could concretely be in a verkle chain context:

1. **Witness generation vs witness verification** — prover side (P) generates Verkle proofs; verifier side (H) hashes/checks them.
2. **P = proof path (KZG commitment/proof computation)**, **H = hash path (Merkle-ization / leaf hashing / chunk hashing)**.
3. **P = peer download path**, **H = local disk/hash path** — e.g., syncing state: downloading witnesses over network (bandwidth B_P) vs hashing/verifying locally (B_H).
4. In stateless validation: block propagation requires sending witnesses; the node's network path (P) and its CPU verification path (H).

Maybe: m is the total number of items (e.g., m chunks of a blob, m leaves of a verkle tree batch). The split q* = m·B_P/B_H means: give q* items to one path and m − q* to the other? Hmm. So maybe q* isn't a count of items but a *threshold ratio*: q* = m·B_P/B_H where m is a multiplier like 1 (or a safety factor), and q* is used differently — e.g., q* is the fraction of the tree depth at which you switch from one path to another, or the checkpoint interval.

Alternatively, maybe the two paths are sequential stages, not parallel splits: path P produces at rate B_P into a buffer; path H consumes at rate B_H. For the pipeline to finish together without stalling, buffer size q* = m·B_P/B_H... Actually in producer-consumer with total transfer m bytes: producer finishes at m/B_P, consumer at m/B_H. If B_P > B_H, consumer is bottleneck. Hmm.

Or: q* is the *queue depth* / window size: to keep both paths busy until they finish together, you need in-flight work q* = m·B_P/B_H. If m is RTT-ish or a chunk count...

Honestly, the formula as stated is what I must take as given: **q\* = m·B_P/B_H**, "a measured split ... that makes two resource paths finish together." So the intended semantics: q* is proportional to the bandwidth ratio. The natural reading: allocate work between two paths in proportion to their bandwidths, scaled by m. If path P gets share ∝ B_P and path H gets share ∝ B_H, then the split *ratio* q* : (m − q*)? No...

The user wrote exactly "q* = m*B_P/B_H". I shouldn't second-guess too hard; I should ground it: define B_P, B_H as measured throughputs, m as total work quantum, and note the exact balanced split is m·B_P/(B_P+B_H), and that q* = m·B_P/B_H is the stated form — perhaps in their regime B_H dominates (B_P + B_H ≈ B_H), i.e., path H is much faster, so the harmonic correction is negligible. Job 1 has remaining work proportional to q*, runs on path P at rate B_P; job 2 has remaining work m, runs on path H at rate B_H. Finish together: q*/B_P = m/B_H → q* = m·B_P/B_H. ✓✓✓

That works perfectly! So: **path H has fixed work m** (e.g., m chunks to hash, m leaves to prove, m slots to fill), and **path P's work q* is chosen** so that both finish at the same instant. E.g., H is the "hard" path with fixed cost m (like KZG proof generation over m points, or hashing m leaves), and P is the adjustable path (like how many witness elements to fetch/verify, or how much padding/prefetch to do). You measure B_P and B_H, compute q* = m·B_P/B_H, and schedule q* units on P so the rendezvous happens.

Concrete instantiation in a verkle chain: 

- **Path H (hash/verify path)**: verifying the block's execution — re-execute m transactions/state accesses against the post-state root. Fixed work m.
- **Path P (proof/provenance path)**: validating the Verkle witness bundle — checking KZG proofs for q* touched keys. Adjustable by batching/granularity.
- The gate: a block is accepted only when both paths finish (rendezvous), giving a single accept timestamp; the split q* ensures neither path idles at the end.

Or in a data-availability context:
- **Path H**: erasure-decode/reconstruct m shards (fixed).
- **Path P**: fetch + KZG-verify q* sampled columns.
Finish together → the provenance gate opens when both done.

OK here's another very natural reading specific to verkle chains and statelessness:

**Stateless seat**: a validator that keeps no state trie. To validate a block it needs witnesses for every touched key. Two ways to get/verify:
- **Path P (peer/network path)**: pull witness sub-trees from peers at bandwidth B_P.
- **Path H (hash/local recompute path)**: recompute/derive parts itself from commitments at rate B_H (CPU-bound KZG checks/hashing).

To have the seat ready exactly when the block arrives (finish together), prefetch q* = m·B_P/B_H witness elements over the network while locally processing m. Something like that.

Given ambiguity, my job per the prompt ("Do the real hard work on this problem, from the exact angle given") is to pick the most defensible concrete semantics, define them crisply, and build the full design: the split law, the rendezvous condition, the persistence/recompute ledger for a dying/respawning stateless seat, all inside a verkle-chain provenance gate. Be exact: numbers, structures, byte layouts, timing formulas, crash matrix.

Let me now design the whole thing properly.

---

## Setting

**Verkle chain facts that matter:**
- State root = Verkle root: a vector commitment (KZG over BN254 or BLS12-381) over 2^w children per node, w=8 or 16 typically (Ethereum's proposal uses width 256, stem-based key layout with 31-byte stems, 256 values per stem).
- Stateless validator verifies block B_n given: parent state root R_{n−1}, the block, and a **witness** W_n containing, for each touched key k: the Verkle proof (KZG opening proofs along the path) + the values. Verification cost is dominated by pairings (~1 pairing per node edge + multipoint eval checks), not by hashing the whole tree.
- Provenance gate: before a seat may act (attest, propose, sign), it must open the gate: demonstrate that every value it relies on traces to R_{n−1} via valid Verkle proofs, i.e., provenance-checked. Gate output: a bit + a gate receipt (hash of verified witness set + root).

**Two resource paths** (I'll fix this now):
- **Path P — proof/witness path**: ingest + verify the Verkle witness bundle arriving from the network (or produced by a co-located prover). Rate B_P = verified-witness-units/sec. Work is tunable: the bundle can be sliced into q units (per-stem proof groups).
- **Path H — hash/execution path**: re-execute the block body: m state accesses (SLOAD-equivalents), signature checks, gas metering — deterministic recompute at rate B_H = access-items/sec. Work m is fixed by the block contents.

Rendezvous requirement: the provenance gate opens only when **both** paths finish; we want them to finish **together** (no tail idle), so the gate latency is minimized and the seat's attest slot isn't missed. Given m fixed on H, choose q (units fed to P) such that q/B_P = m/B_H ⇒ **q* = m·B_P/B_H**. Exactly the given law. 

So the semantics lock in cleanly: **m = fixed work on the hash/execution path; q* = sized work on the proof/witness path so both terminate at t_rendezvous = m/B_H = q*/B_P.**

This is coherent and I'll commit to it. m is measured (number of touched stems/accesses in the block), B_P and B_H are measured online (EWMA of observed rates), q* is computed and enforced by the scheduler that slices the witness stream.

Edge cases to handle exactly:
- If q* > available witness units Q_avail (block touches fewer stems than q*): then P finishes early; to keep rendezvous you either pad P with extra verification (re-check proofs redundantly — useful as Byzantine insurance) or throttle P. Better: define q* as a *target slice size* and clamp: q_run = min(q*, Q_avail), and if clamped, H becomes the critical path — fine, gate opens at m/B_H anyway; the "finish together" is achieved by construction whenever Q_avail ≥ q*.
- If B_P < B_H·(Q_avail/m)... whatever — handle via the same clamp logic.
- Measured rates drift mid-block: re-slice at checkpoints (see below).

Units: make it concrete. Say B_H ≈ 50k stem-accesses/s (re-execution), B_P ≈ 12k proof-groups/s (each group = one stem's KZG openings, ~4 pairings each). m = 24,000 accesses → q* = 24000 × 12000/50000 = 5,760 proof groups. t_rendezvous = 480 ms. Good, concrete numbers.

---

## Now the real meat: stateless seat that dies and respawns — what persists vs recomputes

A "seat" = the process/context holding the slot (validator/prover seat). It dies (OOM, preemption, spot reclaim, deliberate recycle) and respawns (same identity/key, fresh memory). Design goal: after respawn, the seat must reach gate-open state again with minimal redo, and never violate the provenance gate (never attest on unverified provenance).

Key principle: **persist only what is (a) expensive to recompute AND (b) cheap to verify, plus (c) the minimal monotone progress markers needed to avoid redoing network I/O. Recompute everything derivable from persisted roots + inputs. Never persist unverified intermediate state.**

### What persists (durable, across death)

Keep this list brutally short. Each item must survive crash and be self-authenticating or trivially re-verifiable:

1. **Identity & keys**: seat private key / BLS keystore (encrypted at rest). Obviously.
2. **Chain anchors**: last finalized header hash, parent state root R_{n−1}, current slot/epoch. ~100 bytes. These are the *only* trust anchors; everything else derives from them.
3. **Verkle skeleton cache (optional tier)**: the upper levels of the Verkle tree (say top 2–3 levels of commitments, C₀, C₁ nodes) as *commitments only* (48-byte G1 points), not values. Size: width 256 → level-0: 1×256×48 ≈ 12 KB; level-1: 256×256×48 ≈ 3 MB; level-2: 65 MB. Persist level 0–1 only (≈3 MB) — these change rarely per block and re-fetching them costs network round trips. They're self-authenticating: each child commitment is verifiable against parent via the KZG structure once you have any opening; and ultimately against R_{n−1}. Mark them with the root they belong to; discard on reorg.
4. **Progress journal for the in-flight block** (the crucial one): append-only, fsync'd records of *completed, verified* units:
   - `unit_id` (stem index / shard index),
   - `result_digest` = H(unit inputs ‖ unit outputs),
   - for P-path units: the verified proof-group digest,
   - for H-path units: the resulting leaf-value writes as a delta list (key → new value) with running delta-root.
   This journal is what lets a respawned seat skip finished units. It must contain enough to *verify* a unit was done without redoing it: store the digest, not the full data — except for deltas, which you need the actual values for (they feed the final state transition). So: persist actual post-values for executed accesses (they're small: 32 B each) + digests for pure-verification units.
5. **Measured rates**: EWMA state for B_P, B_H (two floats + counts). Cheap to persist, annoying to re-measure cold (cold-start mis-sizing wastes one block cycle). Persist (B̂_P, B̂_H, sample counts, timestamps).
6. **Gate receipts already earned**: for any prior block whose gate opened, the receipt (root, witness-set merkle/verkle digest, timestamp, sig) — needed for slashing-protection and for proving provenance lineage later. Append-only log.
7. **Slashing/finality bookkeeping**: last signed slot, etc. Standard.

Explicitly NOT persisted: any unverified fetched data, partial KZG proof buffers, mempool-derived guesses, the witness bundle raw bytes beyond what's needed for pending verification (actually — see below, there's a nuance: you DO want to persist the raw received-but-unverified witness slices? No — rule: never persist unverified data; on respawn, re-fetch. Network refetch is cheaper than trusting disk garbage. Exception: if fetch is the expensive part (B_P is network-bound), persisting raw slices with a content address and verifying lazily is better than refetch. Decide: persist raw slices keyed by content-address (sha256), tagged `unverified`, cap the pool at, say, 64 MB, evict LRU. On respawn, verify from disk instead of network. This is justified because the *verification* is CPU-cheap relative to refetch when B_P is network-limited. I'll include this as a bounded, tagged cache — clearly marked unverified, never trusted until the journal entry lands.)

### What recomputes on respawn

Everything else, and specifically in this order:

1. Re-derive the working set from anchors: which block n is in flight, re-read block body from local p2p cache or refetch (block body is small; refetch is fine).
2. Recompute m (count of touched stems) — trivial scan of the block.
3. Recompute q* from persisted (B̂_P, B̂_H) and fresh m.
4. Resume scheduling: for each unit, consult journal — done? skip. Else redo.
5. Re-open the gate: replay verification of any units whose journal entries exist but whose *continuity* can't be established (see crash-consistency below) — the journal gives digests; the respawned seat must re-verify at least the *chain* of results: specifically, recompute the running delta-root from persisted deltas (cheap: hashing), and re-check the final root equals expected post-state root R_n claimed by the block. If mismatch → the journal is suspect → fall back to full recompute of affected range. This is the soundness hinge: **persistence is an optimization; correctness always bottoms out in re-deriving R_n from (R_{n−1}, block, witness).**

### Crash-consistency mechanics (exact)

- Journal writes: append record → fsync → mark unit done in RAM. On respawn, a record without fsync completion is ignored (torn tail detected by length+CRC per record; CRC32C + length prefix; truncate torn tail).
- Ordering hazard: H-path delta values must be journaled *with* the digest atomically (single record), else a respawn could apply values whose verification digest was lost → force re-execution of those accesses (safe fallback, just slower).
- Idempotence: every unit's re-execution must be idempotent given (R_{n−1}, block, witness) — true because execution is deterministic; journal skip is safe iff the recorded result_digest matches the digest the current code would compute. Include a **code-version tag** in each journal record; on respawn, records with mismatched version are discarded (software upgraded between death and respawn → those units recompute). This is non-negotiable: digests are only comparable within a version.
- Reorg: any journal tied to a root that's no longer canonical is dropped wholesale (compare anchor).

### The respawn timeline (exact steps, with budgets)

t=0: process dies. Disk retains: anchors, journal, skeleton cache, rate EWMAs, raw-slice pool.
t+r (respawn, r ≈ process start ~200 ms):
1. Load anchors; validate against a beacon/finalized checkpoint (2 headers, ~1 KB). 
2. Scan journal tail (bounded: last N=10⁵ records, ~ tens of MB max) → rebuild done-set bitmap. Cost: ~50 ms for 10⁵ records at 2 GB/s seq read + CRC.
3. Refetch/resume witness stream for missing units; resume execution for missing accesses.
4. Recompute q* = m·B̂_P/B̂_H; re-slice remaining work: remaining P-work q_rem = q* − done_P, remaining H-work m_rem = m − done_H; keep rendezvous: schedule so q_rem/B̂_P ≈ m_rem/B̂_H. Note: after respawn the *new* rendezvous time is max(q_rem/B_P, m_rem/B_H) — the split law re-applied to remainders. If the death happened mid-flight, the original simultaneous-finish is broken; the law is re-established on remainders. That's the right behavior: **q\* is a control law applied to remaining work, not a one-shot constant.**
5. Gate opens when done-set covers all units AND delta-root == R_n. Attest.

Budget claim: with journal hit-rate ρ (fraction of units done before death), respawn adds O(journal scan) + skipped-network-for-done-units; wall-clock to gate ≈ r + max((1−ρ)q*/B_P, (1−ρ)m/B_H) + scan. With ρ=0.6, m=24k, q*=5760: ≈ 200 ms + 192 ms + 50 ms ≈ 442 ms vs 480 ms clean run — i.e., a mid-cycle death costs less than a full redo. Good, concrete.

### Interaction with the provenance gate — the soundness rules

The gate must never open on respawned shortcuts unless:
- Every skipped unit has a version-matched, CRC-valid journal record whose digest chains into the final delta-root;

Per block cycle, worst case persisted growth:
- Journal: m + q* records; record ~96 B (id 8 B, digest 32 B, version 4 B, type 1 B, CRC 4 B, padding) + delta values 32 B each for H-units → m=24k H-records ×128 B ≈ 3 MB + q*=5760 P-records ×48 B ≈ 0.28 MB. ~3.3 MB/block. Prune on finalize (keep only gate receipts + anchors). Trivial.

### Failure matrix (what breaks and the recovery)

- Death during P-unit verify → no journal record → redo that unit. Safe.
- Death during H-unit exec → either atomic record exists (skip) or not (redo). Redo is safe (deterministic).
- Torn journal tail → CRC fail → truncate to last good record. Safe.
- Version skew → drop mismatched records. Safe.
- Disk corruption of delta values → Δroot ≠ R_n → discard journal for block, full recompute. Safe (detected).
- Disk corruption of P-digests w/o checkpoint sig → audit sample catches with prob 1−(1−ε)^bad_count... state it: sampling 1/32 of s skipped units detects ≥1 bad with probability 1−(31/32)^b; for b=10 bad, ≈27%. Commit to: no sig ⇒ re-verify all P-units (cost = one B_P pass, acceptable since death-without-checkpoint is the rare path).
- Reorg between death and respawn → drop journal, restart from canonical anchor.
